 Louisiana Baptist Firment faces runoff, one of two key remaining national races 
 November 20, 2026 
 Early voting, Nov. 28-Dec. 5 
 Election day, Dec. 12 
 By staff
 BATON ROUGE, La. (LBM) – Two key runoff races, of national importance, will be determined on Dec. 12, when voters cast the final ballots for who will represent Louisiana from the U.S. 5th and 6th Congressional Districts.
 Early voting will be open, Nov. 28-Dec. 5.
 State Representative Blake Miguez (R) faces Chauna Banks (D), a staff member with East Baton Rouge Parish Public Schools, in CD-6, encompassing Ascension, Assumption, East Baton Rouge, West Baton Rouge, Iberville, Livingston, Point Coupee, St. John and St. Martin Parishes.
 Meanwhile, state Rep. Gabe Firment (R) and his colleague in the House, Rep. Pat Moore (D), are vying to lead CD-5, which stretches across all or parts of 24 parishes (Avoyelles, Caldwell, East Caroll, West Carroll, Catahoula, Concordia, East Feliciana, West Feliciana, Franklin, Grant, Jackson, La Salle, Lincoln, Madison, Morehouse, Ouachita, Rapides, Richland, St. Helens, St. Landry, Tangipahoa, Tensas, Washington and Winn).
 Gabe Firment 
 Firment, a deacon and Sunday school teacher with First Baptist Church, Pollock, is one of three Louisiana Baptists who ran for Congress in the Nov. 3 General Election.
 Representative Mike Johnson, member, Cypress Baptist Church, Benton, won reelection handily with 58% of the vote in CD-4. Rick Edmonds, pastor, First Baptist church, McComb, Mississippi, and retired pastor, Calvary Baptist Church, Shreveport, lost his bid to represent CD-6, placing third to Banks and Miquez. Firment and Moore took the top two spots in their CD-5 contest.
 In Louisiana, a candidate must win more than 50% of the vote to win the election. Otherwise, a runoff election is held between the two top vote-getting candidates, which is the case for CD-5 and CD-6.
 Nationally, Democrats took control of both chambers of Congress. According to the Associated Press, Democrats won the Senate by 56-44. The two Louisiana races will determine if the Democrats’ House majority, 258-173, so far, increases or not, along with two races, one in Minnesota and another in North Carolina, which have recounts underway.
